NONE: › to get or produce something, especially information or a reaction
引出，探出，誘出（尤指資訊或反應）

example: Have you managed to elicit a response from them yet?
你設法探到他們的反應了嗎？
The questionnaire was intended to elicit information on eating habits.
該調查問卷旨在收集人們飲食習慣方面的資訊。
They were able to elicit the support of the public.
他們獲得了大眾的支持。

NONE: › to not pronounce a particular sound in a word
省略（詞的部分）發音

example: The "t" of "acts" is often elided if someone is speaking quickly.
說話快的時候，人們常常省略「acts」中的「t」音。

NONE: C1 having the necessary qualities or satisfying the necessary conditions
具備條件的；有資格的；合格的
› An eligible person is not married and is thought to be a suitable future marriage partner, especially because they are rich and attractive.
（作爲結婚對象）理想的，合適的

example: Are you eligible for early retirement/maternity leave?
你符合提前退休／休産假的條件嗎？
You might be eligible for a grant.
你或許有資格得到獎學金。
Only people over 18 are eligible to vote.
只有18歲以上的人才有資格投票。
I can think of several eligible bachelors of my acquaintance.
在認識的人當中我能想到有幾位條件不錯的單身漢。

T: C1 [ T ] to remove or take away someone or something
T often passive: C1 [ T often passive ] to defeat someone so that they cannot continue in a competition

example: A move towards healthy eating could help eliminate heart disease.
養成健康的飲食習慣有助於消除心臟病誘因。
We eliminated the possibility that it could have been an accident.
我們排除了這或許是一埸意外事故的可能性。
The police eliminated him from their enquiries.
員警已把他排除在調查對象之外。
He was eliminated in the third round of the competition.
他在第三輪比賽中被淘汰。
A police officer was accused of helping a drug gang eliminate rivals.
一名員警被指控幫助一個販毒黑幫鏟平敵對幫派。

NONE: C2 the process of removing something
排除；消除，清除；淘汰
› by removing from several possible answers the ones that are unlikely to be correct until only one is left
使用排除法

example: the elimination of disease/pain
消除疾病／解除疼痛
their elimination from the competition
他們被淘汰出局
We eventually found the answer by a process of elimination.
我們最終運用排除法得到了答案。

NONE: › a chemical reaction in which a substance separates from a molecule
脫去反應，消去反應（一種物質從分子中分離的化學反應）
› a competition in which only the winners of each stage play in the next stage, until one competitor or team is the final winner
淘汰賽
› a part of a competition in any game or sport where one person or team plays against another to decide which of them will continue to the next stage and which will be removed from the competition
淘汰賽
› the fact of not pronouncing a particular sound in a word
（詞的部分）發音省略
C1 the richest, most powerful, best-educated, or best-trained group in a society
（社會）上層集團；掌權人物；出類拔萃的人，精英
› belonging to the richest, most powerful, best-educated, or best-trained group in a society
（社會）上層集團的；掌權人物的；精英的

example: the country's educated elite
這個國家受過良好教育的精英
a member of the elite
上層集團的一員
disapproving A powerful and corrupt elite has bled this country dry.
該國專權腐敗的權貴階層榨乾了人民的血汗。
Elite troops were airlifted to the trouble zone.
精銳部隊被空運到騷亂地區。

NONE: › organized for the good of a few people who have special interests or abilities
精英統治的；精英主義的
› someone who believes that some things should be controlled or owned only by the richest or best educated people
傑出人物統治論者，精英論者

example: Many remember sport at school as elitist, focusing only on those who were good at it.
在很多人的記憶中，學校體育的導向是精英主義的，被關注的僅僅是那些有特長的人。
They were elitists who had a contempt for popular politics.
他們是精英論者，對大眾政治不屑一顧。

NONE: › a substance, usually a liquid, with a magical power to cure, improve, or preserve something
（通常爲液體的）萬靈藥，靈丹妙藥，長生不老藥

example: It's yet another health product claiming to be the elixir of life/youth (= something to make you live longer/stay young).
這又是一種號稱靈丹妙藥的保健産品，據說有延年益壽／永保青春之奇效。

NONE: › from the period when Queen Elizabeth I was the ruler of England (1558-1603)
（英國女王）伊莉莎白一世時代的(1558-1603)
› a person living during this period
伊莉莎白一世時代的英國人

example: Sir Francis Drake was a famous Elizabethan.
法蘭西斯·德雷克爵士是伊莉莎白一世時代的一位赫赫有名的人物。
